conceptual assets.information: The general-purpose register values held by the register file, on which CPU operand reads and subsequent execution depend. Writeback data enters the stored contents and selected register values leave through the operand outputs.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The register values can be exposed through rs1_o, rs2_o and rs3_o after being read from the stored array (lines 88-89, 126-127 and 141), so an integrator may require confidentiality. The write paths accept rd_i into the stored register contents (lines 86 and 110), allowing unauthorized overwrites that compromise integrity.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe operand outputs to disclose register values or alter writeback data and controls to overwrite registers.

conceptual assets.information: The selected register index used for the write destination or the first source-operand read. Correct CPU behavior depends on this selection addressing the intended register.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The address-selection logic chooses the register array index for a write or first-operand read (lines 78-80, 86 and 88), so changing it can redirect an update or return the wrong register and compromise integrity.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the control fields selecting the register address, causing writes to modify an unintended register or reads to supply an unintended operand.

considered, not kept.concept: Register-access command fields and write enable
considered, not kept.reason: The register-select, direction and write-enable information is an access command on the control record, and the decoded write enable only permits the register to take written data, so Access command fields treats it as part of the access rather than an independent piece (lines 76-80, 85 and 109).
The third-source address is only a slice copied from ctrl_i.ir_funct12 and therefore carries that control-record field rather than forming a separate piece under the Slices rule (line 144).
clk_i only times register updates and rstn_i only resets stored values and outputs, so the Clocks and resets rule excludes them as conceptual assets (lines 84, 106, 108, 122 and 125).

RST_EN, RVE_EN and RS3_EN only select implementation, register-file size or feature generation at build time and cannot be changed or withheld at run time (lines 31-35, 68-69, 98-99, 102-103, 136-149).
